definition: To grope, fondle, or engage in heavy petting; sexually touching a partner's body in an exploratory way, typically stopping short of intercourse.
notes: Also has a non-sexual meaning of fumbling or fiddling with objects; the sexual connotation is primary in youth slang and derives from the image of clumsy, exploratory touching.

definition: To aggressively hit on or persistently pursue someone romantically or sexually; to make overt, repeated advances with the aim of picking someone up.
english_term: to hit on / to pick up
notes: Derived from 'Bagger' (excavator); the metaphor is of digging or scooping someone up; implies persistence and overtness rather than subtle flirting; common in colloquial youth speech.

definition: To grope or grab at someone sexually, with a strong default connotation of unwanted or non-consensual touching; to paw at or molest.
notes: Became a high-frequency media and legal term during German #MeToo discourse (2017–2018); can occasionally be used playfully between consenting partners but carries negative default valence; onomatopoeic quality from the grabbing motion.

definition: To cop a feel from or grope someone; the 'ab-' prefix adds completion and intentionality to the groping act, implying something is snatched or taken from the victim.
english_term: to cop a feel / to grope
notes: Less frequent than 'grapschen'; the separable prefix 'ab-' reinforces the completed, deliberate, and appropriative nature of the act, strengthening the non-consensual implication.

definition: To feel up or thoroughly grope someone; a more intensive and comprehensive version of 'fummeln,' implying systematic or persistent touching of the body.
notes: The 'be-' prefix creates a sense of covering something completely; 'befummeln' thus implies more comprehensive or insistent fondling than 'fummeln'; can carry either consensual or non-consensual connotations depending on context.

definition: To make out or snog; the standard colloquial German term for prolonged passionate kissing with accompanying physical intimacy, typically stopping short of intercourse.
notes: One of the most universally recognized German sexual-register words across all age groups; onomatopoeic quality evokes the smacking sound of kissing; used without register friction in everyday conversation, journalism, and fiction.

definition: To cuddle, snuggle, or be affectionately physical with a partner; implies tender closeness, kissing, and gentle physical contact with a warm emotional tone rather than explicit sexuality.
english_term: to cuddle / to smooch / to snuggle
notes: Warmer and more affectionate in register than 'knutschen'; applies equally to romantic partners and to pets; the implicit sexual charge is mild; originates from Yiddish 'schmusen' (to chat fondly), entering German via urban Jewish communities.

definition: To thoroughly snog or make out with someone; a more emphatic and completed form of 'knutschen,' often implying a prolonged or enthusiastic kissing session with a specific partner.
english_term: to snog / to make out with
notes: The prefix 'ab-' adds a sense of completeness and direction; typically used transitively in 'jemanden abknutschen' (to snog someone); slightly more emphatic and colloquially expressive than plain 'knutschen.'

definition: Open-mouthed kissing with tongue contact; an English loanword used in German to specify tongue kissing as distinct from a closed-mouth kiss.
notes: Capitalized as a noun per German orthographic convention; fully naturalized; specifies tongue-to-tongue contact more precisely than native German alternatives; written as two words (French Kiss) in German usage.

definition: Tongue kisses; the native German compound word for French kissing, denoting open-mouthed kisses involving tongue contact between partners.
notes: Plural form; singular is 'Zungenkuss'; transparent compound: 'Zunge' (tongue) + 'Küsse' (kisses); carries no inherent vulgarity and is used freely in romantic writing, health education, and everyday speech.

definition: To engage in petting; a dated German phrase combining the English loanword 'petting' with 'machen' (to do), referring to sexual caressing and touching short of intercourse.
notes: Borrowed from American 1950s–60s dating culture and widely used in West German youth discourse of the 1960s; strongly associated with the sexual reform literature of that era; largely supplanted in current use by 'knutschen,' 'herummachen,' and more specific slang.

definition: Manual stimulation of the penis performed by a partner; an English loanword fully integrated into German sexual slang.
notes: Identical to the English source term; used casually in everyday speech, social media, and pornographic contexts without register friction; coexists with the native 'Handbefriedigung' (clinical) and 'einen wichsen' (crude).

definition: Mammary intercourse; the act of thrusting the penis between a partner's breasts to stimulation or orgasm.
notes: Compound of crude 'Titten' (tits) and 'Fick' (fuck); mapped to 'frottage' as the closest registry concept covering non-penetrative genital-against-body friction; primarily encountered in pornographic discourse and crude peer-group speech.

definition: To perform mammary intercourse; the two-word verb phrase for thrusting the penis between a partner's breasts, more syntactically explicit than the single compound 'Titfick.'
notes: Functionally synonymous with 'Titfick'; the split verbal form feels cruder and more graphic in context; 'Titten' (tits) + 'ficken' (to fuck); mapped to 'frottage' as the closest registry concept.

definition: Literally 'to push/shove'; used as a colloquial German euphemism for having sexual intercourse, especially in the fixed phrase 'eine schieben' (to have a quickie).
notes: Most commonly found in the fixed construction 'eine schieben'; fading among younger speakers and skewing toward older cohorts; the mechanical push-metaphor parallels similar euphemisms across European languages.

definition: Literally 'to press/squeeze'; used as a vague, contextual German euphemism for sexual activity, particularly grinding or pressing physical contact.
notes: Far less established as sexual slang than 'schieben' or 'ficken'; the sexual reading requires strong contextual cues and is understood mainly by older or dialectal speakers; not to be confused with the ordinary meanings of pressing a button or pushing through a crowd.

definition: Literally 'to rub'; used in sexual contexts to describe rubbing or grinding genitals against a partner's body without penetration.
notes: Primary meaning is mechanical (to grate, to rub); the sexual usage is descriptive rather than fixed slang and depends entirely on context; more likely to appear in erotic narration than in everyday sexual vocabulary.

definition: To fiddle, grope, or fondle in a furtive or clumsy manner; in sexual contexts, persistent or stealthy touching and fondling of a partner's body.
english_term: to fiddle with / to fondle / to grope
notes: Implies a somewhat furtive or adolescent quality — associated with inexperienced or sneaky sexual touching; regional dialectal variants exist; closely related to 'fummeln' but with a slightly more secretive and persistent connotation.

definition: Semen; the dominant everyday German word for the male ejaculatory fluid, used across clinical, educational, and colloquial registers without significant friction.
notes: The default German word for semen; more technical-sounding than English 'cum' but less clinical than 'Ejakulat'; in everyday usage, conflates the fluid with the gametes as English speakers conflate 'sperm' and 'semen'; from Greek 'sperma' (seed).

definition: Ejaculate; the strictly clinical German term for the seminal fluid expelled during orgasm, used primarily in medical, biological, and formal sexological contexts.
notes: Rarely encountered outside academic papers, medical literature, or formal sexual health communication; the -at suffix marks it as a clinical substance-noun; far less common than 'Sperma' in everyday speech.

definition: Seed; a semi-formal or literary German word for semen, rooted in the agricultural and biblical metaphor of the male 'seed' that impregnates.
notes: Primary meaning is botanical seed; as a synonym for semen, it is formal, literary, or dated in register; widely understood due to biblical and classical usage ('des Mannes Samen'); 'Samenzelle' (seed cell) is the standard clinical compound for spermatozoon.

definition: Seminal fluid; a clinical German compound denoting the liquid component of semen, distinguishing the fluid medium from the sperm cells it carries.
notes: Compound: 'Samen' (semen/seed) + 'Flüssigkeit' (fluid); used in medical and biological texts to specify the fluid vehicle; occasionally applied to pre-ejaculate in clinical contexts; rarely heard outside professional or educational settings.

definition: Spermatozoon; the clinical singular term for one individual male sperm cell, the haploid gamete capable of fertilizing an ovum.
notes: Strictly technical and biological; rarely used outside textbooks, medical literature, and university-level education; the plural 'Spermien' is encountered more frequently in everyday health discourse; not used in colloquial speech.

definition: Spermatozoa; the standard clinical and educational plural term for male sperm cells, used in biology, reproductive medicine, and fertility discussions.
notes: Plural of 'Spermium'; more commonly encountered than the singular in everyday health contexts, e.g., 'Spermienanzahl' (sperm count) and 'Spermienmotilität' (sperm motility); recognition boosted by inclusion in school biology curricula.

definition: Ejaculation; the German compound for the act or event of ejaculating, literally 'seed outpouring,' used across clinical, journalistic, and everyday registers.
notes: Compound: 'Samen' (semen/seed) + 'Erguss' (outpouring, gush); occupies a middle register — more euphemistic than 'Ejakulation' and less crude than 'abspritzen'; frequently used in health education materials and mainstream journalism; the 'Erguss' component also means emotional outpouring in literary German, giving the word a slightly poetic quality.
